sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a little round prehistoric turtle with a domed olive-green shell patterned with honey-yellow plates, a cream belly, green spotted skin and four stubby legs, standing turned a little to the left, its head out on its neck. Draw this exact turtle as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the domed shell with its honey-yellow plates and olive-green rim, and the round cream belly below and in front of it, turned as in image 1, without head, without neck, without legs and without tail: no legs or feet drawn on it, the cream belly one smooth round shape. At the front, just above the cream belly and under the shell's front rim, only the very base of the neck comes out of the body: a short stump of green spotted skin, about half as tall as the neck is wide, as wide as the neck is where it meets the body in image 1, ending in a soft edge cut straight across with NO outline (the neck tucks under it). The shell's front rim is drawn whole over it.
2. the body closed up, the turtle hiding: exactly the same shell and cream belly, the same size, but with no neck, no head and no legs showing: under the shell's front rim only a small dark rounded opening where the head went in; the shell's rim and the belly drawn whole and closed all round.
3. the neck alone: the short thick neck of image 1, green spotted skin behind and the cream throat in front, drawn whole from its base (normally hidden in the body) up to just under the head, without the head; both of its ends a soft edge cut straight across with NO outline, the dark outline running only down its two sides.
4. the head alone, without neck: the big round head with its rounded snout, its two little nostrils, its darker green spots and its rosy cheek, turned as in image 1, with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth and no mouth line, the snout and the cream chin one smooth shape. Keep its dark outline over the top of the head, round the snout and along the chin, as in image 1. From the chin round to the back of the head its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline: the cream throat and the green back of the head simply stop there, a little below the rosy cheek.
5. the far front leg: the stubby leg on the far left of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden behind the cream belly) down to its round foot with its soft, round, blunt cream toenails, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
6. the near front leg: the stubby leg in the middle of image 1, in front of the belly, drawn whole from its round shoulder down to its round foot with its soft, round, blunt cream toenails, its round shoulder with its whole outline as in image 1.
7. the near hind leg: the stubby leg on the right of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its thigh (normally hidden under the shell) down to its round foot with its soft, round, blunt cream toenails, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
8. the far hind leg: the same stubby hind leg of the other side, a little smaller as it is farther away, drawn whole from the top of its thigh to its round foot; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
9. the tail: the short pointed-but-soft green tail of image 1, drawn whole from its base (normally hidden under the shell) to its rounded tip; its base a soft edge cut straight across with NO outline.
10. a small bright-green fern leaf: one little frond with a short stalk and soft rounded leaflets, about as long as the turtle's head is wide, in the same style.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no claws. No ground, no text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a little round prehistoric turtle; image 2 shows the same turtle cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the turtle's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the turtle in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, near the snout) is smaller than its near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look up and to the left: each dark-brown iris sits towards the upper left of its eye, the white on its right.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the smaller eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a big dark-brown round iris with a white sparkle, looking up and to the left.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, a warm-brown iris with a white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U.
4. sad: open and round, a soft warm-brown iris with a white sparkle and a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim, looking a little down and to the left; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the bigger eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, up and to the left, the iris towards the upper left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, mouths, without the nostrils, none with any teeth: 17. the mouth as it is in image 1: a thin, closed, sweetly smiling line curling up at its right end. 18. the mouth wide open in a big happy laugh, rounded, the inside pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth. 19. the mouth open in a small round 'o', the inside pink. 20. the mouth in a small sad frown. 21. the mouth wide open in a big round 'O', as for a big yawn, the inside pink with a little tongue, no teeth. 22. the mouth sobbing: a small open downturned frown with a little pink inside. 23. the mouth munching: closed, a short wavy smiling line with the cheek pushed up, chewing.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a little round prehistoric turtle standing turned a little to the left; image 2 shows the same turtle cut into puppet parts. Draw one single piece, centred on the sheet: the turtle's body, without head, without legs and without tail, the same drawing style, colours, texture and line as in images 1 and 2, at the size it has in image 1: the domed olive-green shell with its honey-yellow plates and its rim exactly as in image 1, and below it the cream belly — and at the front, on the left, the big round cream chest of image 1 that bulges forward well in front of the shell's front rim, below where the neck comes out, down to the bottom of the belly, exactly as in image 1, with its dark outline round its front and bottom. Out of the top of the cream chest, under the shell's front rim, rises the very base of the neck, as wide as the neck is there in image 1: cream throat in front, green spotted skin behind, about as tall as half the neck's width, ending at its top in a soft edge cut straight across with NO outline (the neck tucks under it); between the cream throat and the cream chest there is no line at all. No legs or feet drawn on it, no head, no tail. No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows. Fully transparent background.
